deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1974 notes on 'topologie modérée' (tame topology), written around a question of A'Campo. On the previous page Grothendieck had conjectured an intrinsic description of the 'canonical privileged partition' of a tame space X, i.e. its coarsest canonical stratification, in terms of 'immobile' points. He now proposes a conjectural recursive construction of the canonical privileged partition of a proper tame map f: X → Y, with Y (hence X) compact.

Step 0. Let U be the largest open subset of Y such that (1) U is nonsingular (a manifold in the chosen piecewise category) and (2) X|U → U is a locally trivial fibration. One must prove that Y' = Y − U is a rare (nowhere dense) tame subspace, so dim Y' < dim Y.

Step 1. The connected components of U = Y − Y' are the open leaves of the partition of Y, of dimension dim Y. The leaves of X over them are simply the leaves of the intrinsic canonical partition of V = X|U. Locally on U this partition is the product of U with the canonical partition of a fibre.

Step 2 (frontier condition). Write F_i for these leaves. Their 'boundaries' Φ_i = F̄_i − (V ∩ F̄_i) = F̄_i|Y' must be unions of leaves of X. Footnote 6 notes that one must also prove that the closures F̄_i lie in the tame category.

Step 3 (recursion). Put X' = X|Y' = X − V. The problem reduces to finding the canonical partition of X' → Y', where X' now carries the closed subspaces Φ_i and their finite intersections. Since dim Y' < dim Y, induction applies.

Conclusion. Because of this, the right objects to start with are not bare maps X → Y but maps together with a finite family of given closed subspaces of X. To run the same construction in this generality (replacing X by V), one needs, for a space X with a finite family of closed subspaces, the canonical privileged partition, i.e. the coarsest one, of such a system. Grothendieck suggests this can be done by paraphrasing the construction proposed earlier in connection with A'Campo.

In modern terms this is a canonical coarsest topologically-locally-trivial stratification of a proper definable map, compatible with a finite family of closed definable subsets. It is built by the standard downward induction on the dimension of the base: take the generic locus where the base is smooth and the map is a locally trivial fibration, then recurse on the complement while carrying the frontier sets as extra data.
errors: Gap: the recursion only enforces the frontier condition (Φ_i are unions of leaves) and local triviality of X' → Y' over the strata of Y'. It does not guarantee that the whole map X → Y, including the part X|U near Y', is locally trivial along the strata of Y'. That is a condition on neighbourhoods (Thom/Whitney-type triviality), not on the restriction X' alone, so the coarsest partition of the system (X' → Y', {Φ_i}) need not give a locally trivial partition of f.
Unproved: that Y − U is rare (this needs a Hardt-type generic triviality theorem in the tame category) and that the closures F̄_i are tame. Grothendieck himself flags both.

'Canonical = coarsest' presupposes that a coarsest locally trivial partition exists. For maps, existence of a minimal stratification is delicate in the Thom/Whitney setting; for topological local triviality the minimal one obtained by this greedy recursion is canonical but need not be coarsest in every sense. Not addressed here.

ideas.what: Recursive construction of a canonical stratification of a proper map: take the largest open set of the base where the base is smooth and the map is locally trivial, then recurse on the complement.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical/minimal stratification of a map; Hardt triviality in o-minimal/semialgebraic geometry; Thom–Mather stratified maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (1969–70); Hardt (1980); Teissier and Mather for canonical minimal Whitney stratifications of spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 on tame topology and the existence of canonical 'dévissages' of maps; the details there are only sketched

ideas.what: Necessity of working with spaces or maps equipped with a finite family of closed subspaces, closed under finite intersection, so that the induction closes up.
ideas.modern_name: Stratifications compatible with a finite family of definable subsets (standard in Łojasiewicz, Hardt, van den Dries)

ideas.what: Leaves over the generic locus are locally the product of the base with the intrinsic canonical partition of a fibre.
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic stratification of fibres (cf. King; Sullivan; Goresky–MacPherson intrinsic stratification)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches, but leaves unproved, the existence of a canonical coarsest locally trivial partition of a proper tame map relative to a finite family of closed subspaces. He reduces it to the absolute case of a space with marked closed subspaces, via his conjectural 'immobile points' characterization. Canonical topological stratifications of maps in the o-minimal setting are not a standard settled result, but the core ideas here are standard, and the sketch has the local-triviality gap noted above.
missed.quote: il aurait fallu partir non avec X → Y, mais avec en plus une famille finie de sous-espaces fermés donnés de X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It documents Grothendieck's 1974 thinking that preceded the tame-topology section of Esquisse d'un programme. The mathematics itself is close to Hardt/Thom–Mather technology.

deep.surprise_reason: A standard dimension-induction construction of a stratification of a map, with the usual observation that marked subspaces must be carried along. It is historically interesting as a 1974 precursor of the Esquisse tame-topology programme, but not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the struck word reads 'partition/stratification' and is crossed out; the sense is 'feuilles ouvertes de la partition, de dimension dim Y'.
Last lines: likely 'probablement à faire en paraphrasant celle proposée dans la lettre : A'Campo' rather than 'thèse'. This refers to the earlier 'question relative à A'Campo'.
'sans quoi faire' is doubtful; it may read 'sans quoi faire' or 'comme il faut faire'. The sense is that the finite intersections must also be included.
Left-margin footnote 6 reads roughly: 'Il faudra prouver que les F̄_i (closures) ... soient des sous-espaces de la catégorie [modérée] envisagée.'
